CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right middle finger pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ms. Hill is a 41-year-old female presenting with pain in the right middle finger following a motor vehicle accident that occurred approximately 4-5 days ago on Saturday. The patient reports she was stopped at a four-way stop when she was rear-ended from behind by another vehicle. The impact was minor with minimal trunk damage. Following the accident, the patient became upset and made a gesture toward the other driver but was overly enthusiastic and struck the ceiling of the car with her right middle finger. Denies any other injuries from the incident.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Negative except for right middle finger pain as noted above.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atrial fibrillation

MEDICATIONS
Digoxin

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not documented

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Examination reveals tenderness on palpation over the distal phalanx of the right middle finger. Direct pressure over the distal phalanx elicits pain. No pain with palpation of the lower finger. Remainder of examination unremarkable.

RESULTS
X-ray of the right middle finger demonstrates a distal phalanx fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger. Plan includes: (1) Tramadol 50 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain, 8 tablets dispensed; (2) Finger splint application; (3) Follow-up x-ray in 2 weeks. Patient counseled that tramadol is safe with her current digoxin therapy.
